newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise as yen firms, Nikkei falls.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise as yen firms, Nikkei falls.

text.p: The yen's resilience and losses in Tokyo stocks boosted SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Wednesday and dealers said the market showed a firm bias amid signs of continued economic weakness.
"Euroyen rose on some hedge buying in swaps and the yen was also strong compared with yesterday," a trader at a U.S. investment house said.
He said the lead March Euroyen contract seemed to have formed a base around the 98.95 level.
It stood at 99.00 at 1105 GMT after trading a 98.95-99.02 range against an IMM close at 98.95. December was at 99.185 against 99.155.
"There should be limits on the upside for the front months because we're trading in a higher range," the trader said.
But a dealer at a Japanese brokerage said the December Euroyen contract could rise by another 10-12 ticks.
"As people grow more confident that the BOJ (Bank of Japan) is not going to raise rates until the end of the year, December could go to 99.25 or even 99.30," he said.

"Right now the chances are slightly better than 50:50 of them not doing anything. The Japanese economy is not on a strong foothold yet," he said, adding that he would buy Euroyen futures on any signs of weakness.
September JGBs ended at 124.85 against a previous 124.48 on very thin volume of 103 lots.
Eurodollar futures snoozed through most of Wednesday's session with the most active December contract ending unchanged against its IMM close at 94.060 on meagre volume of 1,945 lots.
